solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: German prince warning that Belgium has invaded

indicators.note: one thing having invaded another sits inside it, so the Belgium letter goes into the warning word

parts.note: to give warning is to alert someone
B is the international vehicle registration letter for Belgium

explanation.surface: A German royal warns that his neighbour Belgium has been overrun.
explanation.walkthrough: Prince Albert of Saxe-Coburg was Queen Victoria's German husband.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha was a German-born prince consort, husband of Queen Victoria.

clue.text: Sailor was a cannibal though initially in moderation

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
a cannibal ate men

indicators.note: initially means the opening letter is taken from the word though

explanation.surface: A sailor turned cannibal, though he did it in moderation.
explanation.definitionFit: An abatement is a lessening or reduction, a moderation of something.

clue.text: Blazer that guy's put on?

parts.note: the blazer is not a jacket but a fire, and the guy is the effigy of Guy Fawkes burnt on top of it on 5 November

explanation.surface: Which jacket did that man wear?
explanation.walkthrough: On Guy Fawkes Night (5 November) Britons burn a stuffed effigy called a guy; 'Blazer' and 'put on' suggest clothes. The setter is also Guy.
explanation.definitionFit: A large outdoor fire is something that blazes, and an effigy guy is put on top on 5 November.

clue.text: Remove cleaning products from car in sealed boxes

indicators.note: the words box up the answer, which sits among their letters

explanation.surface: Take the detergents out of the car, packed in sealed boxes.
explanation.definitionFit: After washing with a cleaning agent you wash it away with clean water.

clue.text: Judge going round England on vacation kept cool

indicators.note: turning round means the whole string of letters built after it is read backwards
a place on vacation is emptied, so only the first and last letters of England remain

parts.note: food kept cool has been iced

explanation.surface: A judge travels around an England emptied for the holidays, staying calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' looks like a judge on circuit, but it reverses the whole run of England's ends and the cool word together, giving DECIDE read from the back.
explanation.definitionFit: To judge a matter is to settle or resolve it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Cook with communist sister turned up in Oz

parts.note: to do food is to cook it

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the words are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a red is a communist
a nun is a religious sister

explanation.surface: A cook and a communist nun showed up in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' turns REDNUN into NUNDER. Oz is slang for Australia, not the Wizard's land.
explanation.definitionFit: Down Under is a colloquial name for Australia, so the phrase means located there.

clue.text: Conservative Brexiteer means to create split

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative, the British political party
a Brexiteer voted Leave in the 2016 referendum, so is a leaver

explanation.surface: A Tory Brexit supporter intends to cause a party split.
explanation.walkthrough: 'means' looks like a verb (intends), but it is a noun: a tool for splitting.
explanation.definitionFit: A butcher's chopper is a tool for cutting meat apart.

clue.text: Dull Democrat ousted by Republican in dismay

indicators.note: one party ousted by another is replaced, so one letter is swapped for the other

parts.note: dread is fear or dismay
D is the abbreviation for a US Democrat
R is the abbreviation for a US Republican

explanation.surface: A dreary Democrat unseated by a Republican, to his dismay.
explanation.walkthrough: The final D of DREAD is replaced by R.
explanation.definitionFit: Drear is a literary form of dreary, meaning gloomy and uninteresting.

clue.text: Animation script back from printers after second page corrected

indicators.note: after means the script pieces come behind the second-page-corrected pieces

parts.note: something corrected has been put right
an actor's script is their lines

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, here from printers

explanation.surface: A cartoon script comes back from the printers once a second page is fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Animation' suggests cartoons, but here it means liveliness.
explanation.definitionFit: Animation in the sense of vivacity and liveliness is being sprightly.

clue.text: Deploy now and strike

indicators.note: to deploy is to arrange or position, so these two words are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: An order to send troops in now and attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' looks like part of the military order, but it is the definition, in the sense of an idea striking you.
explanation.definitionFit: When a realisation strikes you it dawns on you; both mean to occur to someone's mind.

clue.text: Fine ground supplied with electricity around start of December

indicators.note: the electricity word goes around the December letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a machine supplied with electricity is powered

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, here from December

explanation.surface: An electrified field from early December, ground very fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ground to a fine dust has been reduced to powder, as with powdered sugar.

clue.text: Requiem mass Verdi composed without right notes

indicators.note: music composed is put together, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these three words, less one R, are rearranged

explanation.surface: Verdi wrote his Requiem Mass leaving out the proper notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' signals that the R for right is taken away from the letters of REQUIEMMASSVERDI before they are rearranged; Verdi's Requiem is a real work, which makes the surface convincing.
explanation.definitionFit: A demisemiquaver is a thirty-second note, a very short musical note value.

clue.text: Seafood sandwiches always unpleasantly hot

indicators.note: the seafood word sandwiches the other, holding it between its parts

parts.note: fish is seafood
ever means always, as in ever hopeful

explanation.surface: Seafood sandwiches that have always been unpleasantly overheated.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a fever has an uncomfortably high temperature, so feeling feverish is being unpleasantly hot.

clue.text: Very rude hosts out of bread

indicators.note: the rude word hosts the very letter, taking it in

parts.note: insolent means rude or impertinent

explanation.surface: Very rude party hosts who have run out of bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is slang for money, and someone with no money left to pay debts is bankrupt.

clue.text: Frank's hair colour came to grief in the sea, you'd say

indicators.note: what you would say aloud is a sound-alike of the written letters

parts.words: hair colour came to grief in the sea
parts.note: a hair colour is a dye, and a ship that came to grief at sea was wrecked

explanation.surface: Frank's hair dye apparently suffered a shipwreck.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, DYE WRECKED sounds like the answer. The 's of Frank's is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A frank person is straightforward and candid, which is what a direct person is.

clue.text: Fresh scones for father in box

indicators.note: fresh means new, so these letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: Freshly baked scones for Dad in the lunchbox.
explanation.walkthrough: The box is a confessional, and the father a priest.
explanation.definitionFit: A priest who hears confessions sits in the confessional booth, a box.

clue.text: Social class university fed into data

indicators.note: the university letter is fed into the data word, going inside it

parts.note: stats, short for statistics, are data

explanation.surface: A university feeds social class information into a dataset.
explanation.definitionFit: Status is one's standing or rank in society.

clue.text: A lot of opera, and beer in proportion

indicators.note: a lot of means most of, so the final letter is cut

parts.note: Tosca is Puccini's opera
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: Lots of opera and beer, all in the right measure.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawing made to scale has its dimensions in correct proportion to the original.

clue.text: Learning about wet quiche's origin?

indicators.note: the learning word goes about the wet word, surrounding it

parts.note: lore is traditional learning or knowledge
rain is wet weather

explanation.surface: A lesson about soggy pastry and where the quiche came from.
explanation.walkthrough: Quiche Lorraine is named after the French region it comes from, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The region in north-east France gives its name to the famous egg-and-bacon tart.

clue.text: Excellent doctor saw me more regularly

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are rearranged
regularly means every other letter is taken from the word more

explanation.surface: An excellent doctor saw me more often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes O and E from more; these join SAWME and 'doctor' rearranges all seven.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang, something superb or outstanding is said to be awesome.

clue.text: Kids prepared for dinner, tossed green salad then left

indicators.note: a salad is tossed, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Children who had a dinner prepared, a tossed green salad, then went off.
explanation.walkthrough: In the fairy tale the witch fattens the two children to eat them, so they are 'prepared for dinner', not fed.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Grimm fairy tale the two children are fattened by the witch so she can cook and eat them.

clue.text: Orphaned girl sheared goats

indicators.note: sheared means trimmed, so the first and last letters are clipped off

parts.note: nannies are female goats

explanation.surface: A girl without parents gave her goats a haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Orphan Annie is the American comic strip and musical heroine.
explanation.definitionFit: Little Orphan Annie is a famous fictional parentless girl from comics and the musical.

clue.text: Chart hit used in Mercury Rising

indicators.note: the hit word is used in the other, going inside it
in a down clue, rising means the word is read from the bottom up, backwards

parts.note: Hg is the chemical symbol for mercury
to rap is to hit or knock

explanation.surface: A hit song featured in the film Mercury Rising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns HG to GH; Mercury Rising is a 1998 film, a convincing surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A graph is a diagram plotting data, a kind of chart.

clue.text: Maybe Nike produce tin cups, spending billions

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin

indicators.note: money spent is gone, so the billions letter is taken out

parts.note: beakers are drinking cups
B is a standard abbreviation for billion

explanation.surface: A sports brand manufactures tin mugs at a cost of billions.
explanation.definitionFit: Nike makes trainers, sports shoes that Americans call by this name.

clue.text: Driver used to going at 200mph — mostly unaccompanied, then?

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: unaccompanied means alone
so can mean then, as in 'so you came'

explanation.surface: A speed-loving driver, usually travelling solo: is that it, then?
explanation.walkthrough: Fernando Alonso is a Spanish Formula One racing driver.
explanation.definitionFit: Fernando Alonso is a double Formula One world champion, a racer used to very high speeds.

clue.text: Item nobody wants to take on plane stuffed with cocaine

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading

indicators.note: the plane word is stuffed with the cocaine letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a jet is a plane
C is slang shorthand for cocaine

explanation.surface: Something no traveller wants to carry onto a plane packed with drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A reject is a cast-off, something turned down that nobody will accept.

clue.text: Old high definition audio equipment that's not very good

parts.note: the ear is the body's equipment for hearing

explanation.surface: Ageing hi-def sound gear that isn't up to much.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation expresses mild dismay at something disappointing.
